title: Evening GPU triage logbook
content:
Purpose: quick personal triage notes from the late-evening infra shift. Not polished — dump of commands, outcomes, and follow-ups for morning shift.

SUMMARY (TL;DR):
- Spike in GPU memory OOMs around 21:12 UTC affecting batch-predict route (route: /v1/predict/batch).
- Root cause probable: sudden increase in sequence lengths + 2 hot jobs pinned to same instance pool (nodepool: g3b-large-rt).
- Actions taken: scaled pool by +2 nodes, evicted runaway pods, restarted runtime on gpu-05, added temporary request-size limiter on the route.
- Immediate impact: latency returned to baseline (~95th percentile back to 420ms) by 21:45. No customer-visible errors recorded in Sentry beyond a handful of 429s.

COMMANDS & QUICK OUTPUTS (copy-paste later if needed):
- Check pod statuses (filtered):
  kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep batch-predict
  # saw 3 CrashLoopBackOff, 2 Running but 0/1 ready

- GPU util & temps (snapshot):
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv\  # gpu-05: util 98%, temp 83C, mem 31264 MiB / 32768 MiB

- Runtime logs (tail):
  tail -n 200 /var/log/inference/runtime.log | grep -i oom\  # repeated OOM at 21:11:46 in shard 3 for model-llama-13b-fp16

- Evict & restart sequence used:
  kubectl drain gpu-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data\  # graceful evict, then reboot node via terraform (quick reboot)
  kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n inference --field-selector metadata.name=runtime-deploy

NOTES / OBSERVATIONS:
- Two long-running batch jobs (job IDs PG-1309, PG-1317) were pinned to same instance; both requested max_seq_length=8192 — unusual for this project. Need to flag for model-owner.
- autoscaler did not trigger quick enough because nodepool had min=2, max=4 and burst policy cooldown is 10m (we want to consider lowering cooldown for batch-predict route).
- kernel driver 525.105 was updated last week on these nodes; temperature spikes are on the higher side (82–85C). Not conclusive but worth monitoring.

TO-DO (prio ordered):
- [P0] PM: Add sequence-length check and reject >4096 at API layer for batch-predict until we have autoscaler tuned. (me)
- [P0] Ops: Adjust cluster-autoscaler cooldown for g3b-large-rt pool from 10m -> 3m during business hours. (ticket: JIRA-PG-1309)
- [P1] Infra: Add a placement constraint to avoid co-locating >1 heavy-batch job per node (taint/toleration or topologySpread). (collab: Ivy)
- [P1] SRE: Dashboard: create 1h heatmap for seq_length distribution across routes. (Samir)
- [P2] Follow-up with model team owning PG-1317 about reducing memory footprint or switching to streaming decode.

HANDOFF NOTES (for morning shift):
- Watch for PG-1309 retries >3: escalate to platform-oncall. Slack alert already setup for retry > 5 but not for 3 — consider adding.
- If gpu-05 shows repeated high temp after reboot (>85C) open hardware ticket; might be airflow issue on rack 4.
- Keep an eye on cluster-autoscaler events: kubectl get events -n kube-system | grep autoscaler

QUICK REMINDERS / PERSONAL TODOS: 
- Write short blurb for oncall runbook about how to temporarily apply API-level max_seq guard.
- Add note in Confluence about temporary workaround and link to this file.
- Confirm with infra-procurement re: spare GPUs available (we may want to increase reserved pool next month).

OPEN QUESTIONS / THINGS TO THINK ABOUT:
- Should we automatically reject requests with length > 4096 at the edge, or return a suggested smaller batch split? UX tradeoff.
- Is the autoscaler cooldown tuned for cost or latency? Might need a policy per-route.
- If driver upgrades correlate with temp spikes we should pin to previous driver for suspect nodepool and run A/B.

SNIPPETS TO COPY INTO TICKETS: 
- "Observed repeated GPU OOMs on 2026-03-11 21:11 UTC for model-llama-13b-fp16. Root cause: co-located long seq-length batch jobs + autoscaler cooldown. Temporary mitigation: scale +2 nodes and restart runtime; apply max_seq guard at API."
- Quick repro commands: nvidia-smi; kubectl get pods -n inference; tail -n 200 /var/log/inference/runtime.log | grep -i oom

RANDOM NOTES / brain-dump:
- Might be good to add per-request token estimate in our gateway so we can route heavy requests to dedicated pools automatically.
- Remember to update the 'burst capacity' playbook with the manual node add steps (terraform quick-apply snippet).
- Logstash filter for OOM messages needs to normalize stack traces (we're drowning in repeated lines currently).

END. Will tidy and move to Confluence tomorrow if this stays relevant.

Signed-off: Leah M. (late evening shift)
